adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, `selectedCalendar` is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else-branch), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to `externalCalendarId` (i.e., `undefined`/`null`), so it will not match any real calendar externalId and returns `undefined`. This makes the fallback effectively dead/broken and can lead to attempting an update without a valid calendar id (or at least not selecting the intended destination calendar). The same faulty pattern is also introduced in deleteEvent.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is not supplied (the else-branch), the `.find` predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to the falsy `externalCalendarId` (likely `undefined`/`null`), so it will typically return `undefined`, making `calendarId` undefined rather than falling back to a destination calendar externalId. This is a regression from the previous logic (`... : event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can cause deletes to target no calendar (or force fallback behavior elsewhere), leading to failed deletions/orphaned events as described.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,`). Immediately after, team member calendars are appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: EventManager.ts ~370 no-credentialId branch calls createEvent(c, event) without the new externalId argument, so Google's createEvent credential match fails and falls back to 'primary' (previously used destinationCalendar.externalId), and the returned result.externalId is undefined so booking references get externalCalendarId: undefined — cascading into the broken Google update/delete fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the no-`credentialId` path (`else` under `if (destination.credentialId)`) calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the new `externalId` argument (see the `Promise.all(...map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event)))`). `CalendarManager.createEvent` now only returns `externalId` via that third argument, and `EventManager` later persists `externalCalendarId` from `result.externalId` (changed from `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This means references will store `externalCalendarId: undefined` for these events. Additionally, Google’s `createEvent` now selects the calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when no match exists—exactly the case in the no-credentialId branch—so events may be created on the wrong calendar and subsequent update/delete will lack the externalCalendarId needed to target the right calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: handleCancelBooking.ts ~443 recurring-event branch uses `references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` deleting only the first calendar event per recurring booking (non-recurring path was correctly changed to filter), and EventManager.ts ~540 reschedule-merge path likewise deletes only the first old reference — with multiple _calendar references now normal for collective bookings, recurring/merged collective cancels and reschedules orphan calendar events on every host except the first

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multi-calendar support via `destinationCalendar: DestinationCalendar[]` and multiple `_calendar` references being handled in several places by switching from `find` to `filter` (e.g., `handleCancelBooking` now does `references.filter(...)` for the main deletion path; `EventManager.updateCalendarEvents` now processes `calendarReference` as an array). Similarly, in `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the merge cleanup still uses `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`, so it would delete only the first old calendar reference when multiple exist (now normal for collective/team cases per this PR).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: EventManager.ts ~345-365 createAllCalendarEvents silently skips destinations whose credentialId isn't in calendarCredentials or whose DB fetch yields no credential (dangling/deleted credential or missing app row) — no error, no calWarning, no failed result, so bookings confirm with missing calendar events; same silent-skip pattern in updateAllCalendarEvents' DB fetch; should surface a warning/result

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents, the new loop over `event.destinationCalendar` only calls `createEvent` when a `credential` is found either in `this.calendarCredentials` or via the Prisma `findUnique` fetch. If neither lookup yields a usable credential (e.g., dangling/deleted credentialId or missing `app.slug` so the credential object isn’t constructed), the code simply falls through without pushing any failed `EventResult`, warning, or error for that destination—i.e., the destination is silently skipped (`if (credential) { ... createdEvents.push(...) }` with no else). This matches the finding that bookings could proceed with missing calendar events without surfacing a warning/result.
